title: Overhang test
about: six ledges leaning 20° to 70° from vertical: print without supports and find the angle where your printer starts to droop
tries: Test 45° to 70° in 5° steps instead | Give my printer a 55° overhang limit and show what changes in the job | Explain why the 50° underside is reported and the 40° one is not

agent.role: a print-process engineer who designs test pieces that isolate one printer limit
agent.prompt: Prefer changing the angles list and h over new geometry; keep every ledge the same height so only the angle varies; never add supports or chamfers to the test faces.

fragments.angles: Keep angles in degrees from vertical, the convention of print.overhang and the printer's maxOverhang.
